title: Punt BLK: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt BLK build, and how do they keep us competitive in REB and FG%? It must warn that blocks travel with rebounds and FG%, so chasing only low-block players can sink those two categories too.
summary: Punting blocks fits our 9-cat league because blocks swing a lot from year to year, and the cheap guards Ty Jerome, Immanuel Quickley and Payton Pritchard give threes, assists and FT% with almost no blocks. The catch is that blocks travel with rebounds and FG%. If you pick players only because they block little, you can lose REB and FG% as well, so check every target's FG% and keep real rebounders in your F and C slots.

sections.heading: Why punt BLK, and the catch

paragraphs.text: Blocks are very variable from year to year. The experts rank them with steals, threes and FT% as categories that are fine to punt. Even after punting them, you still win some weeks by surprise. Points and assists are stable, high-volume categories and bad to punt.

Blocks do not move alone. High blocks go with high rebounds and FG%. So if you only chase low-block players, your REB and FG% will drop too. In our league that can turn one punted category into three lost ones every week.

The rule for draft day: punt the blocks, not the bigs. Your C slot and some F and Util slots still need players who rebound and shoot a good FG%. Fill your guard slots with low-block players who bring threes, assists and FT%.

sections.heading: Where the notes pull in different directions

paragraphs.text: The notes do not clash head on, but they lean different ways. One view says blocks are a good punt because they are volatile and you still steal some weeks. The other view is the correlation warning: blocks, rebounds and FG% are the one cluster that moves together, so punting blocks pushes you away from all three. The same expert who calls the big man build hard to run says this cluster is the only thing it gets. Both points hold. Punt BLK is a sound choice, but only if you protect REB and FG% on purpose.

sections.heading: Guard targets at the right price

paragraphs.text: Ty Jerome is the best value. Experts take him as a top 100 player, but his Yahoo average cost is very low. A bid up to 11 USD is fine. He brings 3PM, AST, STL and FT% with almost no blocks. Memphis also has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule. Early on, check that he gets 27 or more minutes and stays healthy.

Payton Pritchard fits for threes, FT%, assists and few turnovers. He has played 79 to 82 games in each of the last three seasons. Bid in the single digits. Do not chase him near the 16 USD our league paid last season.
Immanuel Quickley gives threes and assists at about 5 to 10 USD. His FG% is below average (43.5%). That is exactly the drag the correlation warning describes, so pair him with efficient shooters.

Jalen Brunson fits a punt BLK build that wants points and assists. Category experts value him at about 18 to 20 USD. Our league paid 31 USD last season. He brings almost no rebounds, and the Knicks have a weak playoff schedule for our March 28 end. Let someone else pay 30 USD or more.

sections.heading: Late picks that help protect FG%

paragraphs.text: Use your last 1 USD picks on low-block players who do not hurt FG%. Aaron Gordon is projected at about 52% FG with few turnovers and is eligible at F and C. He played only 36 games last season and keeps having hamstring and calf problems, so pay 1 USD at most or leave him on waivers.

Tre Jones is projected at 54% FG and about 5 assists with few turnovers. He is a bench player with last-pick value, so pay no more than 1 USD or leave him on waivers. If Giddey or Powell gets hurt or Powell is traded, add him with FAB right away.

Saddiq Bey is at the edge of our 144-player pool. The experts call him a fragile bench piece on a crowded roster. Take him only as a 1 USD final pick, and check early whether he starts or closes games.

sections.heading: Checklist for draft day and the first weeks

paragraphs.text: Before each bid, check the player's FG%. A low-block guard with a weak FG%, like Quickley, needs an efficient player beside him. Do not draft a whole roster on the low-block tag alone. Count your rebounders before the last rounds. After the draft, use your 6 weekly adds to fix REB or FG% if they fall behind, and expect to win the odd blocks week by luck.
